note: Europe 1815 after the Congress of Vienna: Austrian Empire, enlarged Prussia, German Confederation states, Congress Poland, United Netherlands, Sweden-Norway.

properties.label: Netherlands
properties.info: The Congress of Vienna created a united kingdom of the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg under the House of Orange.
A Habsburg crown land: Francis I ruled it as king or archduke, in personal union with the Austrian Empire.

properties.label: Switzerland
properties.info: The Swiss Confederation was restored in 1815 with 22 cantons and declared permanently neutral.

properties.label: France
properties.info: The Bourbons were restored in 1814-15 after Napoleon's fall, and France was reduced to roughly its 1790 borders.

properties.label: Tuscany
properties.info: Habsburg-Lorraine Tuscany was restored in 1814.

Naples was restored under Ferdinand IV after Murat's fall; the two kingdoms were merged as the Two Sicilies in 1816.

properties.label: Prussia
properties.info: Prussia was restored in 1815 and gained the Rhineland, Westphalia, Posen, northern Saxony and Swedish Pomerania; it was now the leading power in the German Confederation.

properties.label: Sardinia
properties.info: Restored in 1814, Sardinia regained Savoy and Nice and gained Genoa and Liguria at the Congress of Vienna.
Sicily remained under Bourbon rule through the Napoleonic era, protected by the British; merged with Naples in 1816.

properties.label: Spain
properties.info: Spain was restored under Ferdinand VII after the Peninsular War (1808-14); its American colonies were in revolt.

properties.label: Papal States
properties.info: The Papal States were restored in 1814-15 under Pius VII, including the Legations of Bologna and Ferrara.
Moldavia, reduced after Russia annexed Bessarabia in 1812, was an Ottoman vassal under a Phanariot hospodar.

properties.label: Parma
properties.info: Parma was granted to Napoleon's wife Marie Louise for life.

properties.label: Denmark
properties.info: Denmark lost Norway to Sweden in 1814 but kept Schleswig, Holstein, Iceland and the Faroe Islands.

properties.label: Thuringian states
properties.info: Thuringia was split into many small Saxon duchies and principalities, which joined the German Confederation in 1815.

properties.label: Saxony
properties.info: Saxony, a loyal ally of Napoleon, lost about half its territory to Prussia in 1815.

properties.realm: Free Cities of Hamburg and Bremen
properties.label: Hamburg and Bremen
properties.info: Hamburg and Bremen regained their independence as free cities in 1814-15 after French occupation.

properties.label: Hesse
properties.info: Hesse was divided between the Electorate of Hesse-Kassel and the Grand Duchy of Hesse-Darmstadt, both members of the German Confederation.

properties.label: Hanover
properties.info: Hanover became a kingdom in 1814 and was in personal union with the British crown, gaining East Frisia and Hildesheim.

properties.label: Württemberg and Baden
properties.info: Napoleon's allies Württemberg (kingdom) and Baden (grand duchy) kept their enlarged territories and joined the German Confederation in 1815.

properties.label: Bavaria
properties.info: Bavaria became a kingdom in 1806 under Napoleon and in 1815 joined the German Confederation, gaining the Palatinate in 1816.

properties.label: Austrian Empire
properties.info: The Austrian Empire (proclaimed 1804; Austria-Hungary only came in 1867) included Bohemia, Hungary, Croatia, Transylvania and Galicia, and regained Lombardy-Venetia, Tyrol, Illyria and Galicia at the Congress of Vienna, but gave up the Holy Roman crown in 1806 and the Austrian Netherlands. Bohemia, Hungary, Croatia and Transylvania were ruled in personal union.
These lands remained Ottoman.

properties.label: Congress Poland
properties.info: The Kingdom of Poland, created in 1815 from the Duchy of Warsaw, had its own constitution but was ruled by the Russian tsar as king.
Malta was taken from the French in 1800 and confirmed as British in 1814.

properties.label: Modena
properties.info: The Austrian Archduke Francis IV ruled Modena, Reggio and Massa-Carrara.

properties.label: Lucca
properties.info: Lucca was a small Bourbon duchy under Marie Louise until 1824, when it was absorbed into Tuscany.
Naples was restored under Ferdinand IV after Murat's fall; the two kingdoms were merged as the Two Sicilies in 1816.

properties.realm: United States of the Ionian Islands
properties.label: Ionian Islands
properties.info: The Ionian Islands became a British protectorate in 1815.
Armenia and Nakhchivan were still Persian until 1828.

properties.label: Sweden–Norway
properties.info: Sweden lost Finland to Russia (1809) and Swedish Pomerania, but gained Norway in 1814 in a personal union under one king.
